title: Volume 2 Chapter 4: To You Whose Voice Cannot Reach Me, and to You Whom I Can Touch 2
content: In deep prayer, he offered thanks to God.
Not for the successful retrieval of the Sacred Artifact, but for the safety of Shara Ransura.
Strangely enough, in his mind, the matter of recovering the Sacred Artifact had been settled the moment he had requested the Longdagger Couple to handle it; it was bound to succeed.
Thus, his gratitude to God was for sending those two to this land and for Shara's safe return.
Well, it might be a bit of a stretch to say Shara's return was safe, considering she kept insisting she heard the Voice of God, but at least she was physically unharmed.
Bishop Vival thought it was quite common for members of the Church to fall into such confusion when acting alongside adventurers, so he believed Shara would calm down after a while.
Though he couldn't quite imagine that girl settling down.
That aside, Vival recalled his own embarrassing past and realized he had drifted from his prayer, breaking his posture.
God asks nothing of us humans, but if we are to offer prayers, they must be sincere, he believed.
As his thoughts wandered from prayer, Vival suddenly thought of Shara.
It was indeed fortunate that that unfortunate girl had, by chance, made acquaintances with the Longdagger Couple.
Vival had dedicated his life to God.
He had no regrets about that, but the fact that he had never had children filled him with a profound sense of regret.
Perhaps because of this, he couldn't help but view Shara with the eyes of a father.
A noble adventurer was the perfect companion to entrust Shara, who was a Sister with a peculiar inability in Healing Magic.
If she had received an education befitting a noble, it was certain she would be able to use Healing Magic herself.
When he received the report that Shara had made an enormous donation, he felt his intuition had been remarkably sharp.
He wanted to commend his memory for recalling that the name Longdagger belonged to the husband of the aforementioned Erika Solnzali.
No, rather, it was Shara, who had managed to make acquaintances with such adventurers, who was truly impressive.
Our Sister is amazing, Shara is great, Vival nodded in agreement.
Perhaps it was the fresh air that had made his thoughts scatter, he thought with a wry smile.
He was reminded of his past when he fought alongside adventurers against monsters.
To reward the adventurers who dealt with the horde of monsters that had suddenly overflowed from the Demon Realm, the lord had made drinks free for two days, and the town was in a festive uproar.
In the past, after finishing a request, he too would drink heavily with his companions at the tavern, and Vival felt a sense of nostalgia at the town's merriment.
Still kneeling, lost in thought in the chapel, Vival suddenly turned back as he remembered that praying to God was not only about giving thanks.
He took up his prayer posture once more and offered a sincere prayer.
For the Faltarl Kingdom, which had lost Erika Solnzali and Shin Longdagger.
He prayed for the peace of its future.
Shara Ransura.
A Sister from the Makikomaru Claw Barony.
Although she was terrible at Healing Magic, she claimed her efforts were well-received as a former member of the Healing Faction.
As she walked through the forest of the Demon Realm, she was filled with rage. One could say she was furious.
Had it not been for the miracle of hearing the Voice of God, she might have charged at Shin, fully aware she would lose.
It was because Shin had suggested he doubted the Bishop.
She was angry at the Church of Faltarl for exiling Erika, but she was equally furious at Shin.
"I'm not doubting it anymore."
Shara looked at Shin with suspicion as he shrugged with a wry smile.
She recalled the moment she had been suddenly blown away in the forest of the Demon Realm.
She had been scared.
It was frightening to be alone in the forest, but she was even more terrified that Erika and Shin might think she was unnecessary.
Indeed, she might just be a burden to them.
Even if she was with them, she might not be able to help them at all.
But still, Shara liked these two.
They were reckless in their actions, absurd in their words, and what was worse, their execution was equally chaotic.
Yet, watching them charge headfirst at the absurdities thrown their way felt refreshing.
This world was filled with absurdities everywhere.
Especially for commoners, absurdity was a frequent adversary.
Even someone like her, who had been expelled from the Healing Faction for being terrible at Healing Magic, had managed to stay there for a long time.
Once she stepped out of the town, it was overflowing with absurdity and death.
Those living in villages without barriers could easily die with just a bit of bad luck.
A poor harvest could lead to starvation.
Having been raised in a sheltered environment after being entrusted to the Church as a child, Shara had no real experience with such absurdities.
That was why she considered herself fortunate.
A gift from God.
If she had received such a gift, she wanted to give something back.
That was why Shara had devoted herself to practicing magic since childhood.
She took pride in the effort and time she had invested.
Despite her lack of progress in Healing Magic, she never gave up.
For some reason, her skills in offensive and chant magic had improved to a point that even she found impressive.
All of that was for the Church's doctrine of saving the weak, and she believed that doing so was a way to repay God.
Ideally, she wanted to be active in the Healing Faction.
And then she met the two of them.
They had charged headfirst into a Golden Ogre that would have wiped out the village, taking on the request of a girl they had never met for free.
This was it; she thought these two were it.
Adventurers who shared a similar ideology to the Church, fighting for those who could not fight.
She thought they were the ideal embodiment of that.
If she were to be expelled from the Faction, she would want to be sent to these two.
She never imagined she would actually be expelled and sent to those two.
To be honest, she was shocked when the Bishop told her to change factions.
But when she learned she would be sent to Shin and Erika, she was overjoyed.
She liked those two that much.
She wished she could avoid suddenly gushing about her feelings without any context.
Especially since they were in a situation where a magical tool capable of blowing up the town could explode at any moment, she really wished she could refrain from gushing.
It was genuinely incomprehensible.
It was a bit hypocritical for her, who was nibbling on dried meat due to a slight hunger, to say this, but those two might just lack a sense of common sense.
Ah, no, no, that's not it.
Shara steeled herself and looked up.
Before her were Erika, engulfed in flames, and Shin, cutting down approaching monsters left and right.
Moreover, Shin, bloodied and battered, was gazing at Erika with a smile.
It was a bit unsettling.
Shara felt she had to ask.
Aren't you still doubting the Church and us?
No, that's not it; what she really wanted to ask was this:
Can I not be your comrade?
As she opened her mouth, she hesitated. What came out was a pitiful voice.
"Um, why is it that you 'aren't doubting the Church anymore'?"
She thought she had taken quite a roundabout way to ask that.
The forest was filled with the screams and death throes of monsters, but Shin, who had not missed her voice, turned around and tilted his head while swinging a horned rabbit monster with one hand.
"Why do you ask that?"
His expression seemed to say, "Why would you ask something like that?" and Shara held her breath.
How foolish; there was no way to get the answer she wanted by asking Shin in such a roundabout way.
"If you're angry that your comrade would think such a thing, then I suppose that's how it is."
"Am I your comrade!?"
Shara exclaimed, cutting him off.
"Hey, Erika! Shara is asking if she is our comrade!"
Why does he have that "ugh, how troublesome" face!?
Shara grew angry again.
"I consider Shara to be a comrade! I believe we are friends!"
Yay! Shara cheered in her heart.
"I'm just reluctantly acknowledging it. If you don't like it—"
"I am your comrade!"
Shara declared, interrupting Shin.
What was that? She should have done this from the start. It was such a simple matter.
Especially since Shin seemed to have few friends due to his overwhelming affection for Erika; if she declared herself a comrade, it would surely win him over.
He was an easy person.
"What on earth is going on?"
Shin grumbled as he returned to his work of slicing monsters in half.
"Hey, hey! Shin! When did you consider me a comrade!?"
Shara skipped closer to the two.
She cast a spell, fully aware that she might not be of much help.
When could it have been? Perhaps when they all entered the Demon Realm together?
Or maybe when they were all trying to escape the explosion radius of that Rainibati thing?
No, perhaps it was when they realized she was not a traitor.
"Eh?"
Come on, don't make that troublesome face and answer me.
Shara urged Shin with her gaze.
When Shin momentarily looked off into the distance, he murmured softly that being angry because he thought she had betrayed him was proof that it was real.
What could that mean? Shara tilted her head.
She wished he would stop saying such complicated things, especially since he was a barbarian.
Shin was looking at her with a gentle expression. Was he going to give her some meat?
"It was when you were gnawing on dried meat in that hole."
"Why!?"
Shara exclaimed loudly. It was frustrating but also fun.

In the forest of the Demon Realm, beside the Demon Church, in a hastily dug hole, for the first time in her life, Erika Solnzali realized she had accepted death the moment she heard the sound of space shattering.
Various thoughts surged within her.
If only she had just a little more magical power, she could think of her best friend in the royal capital, her parents.
Strangely enough, the resentment of being exiled hardly surfaced; she only thought that she wished that damn prince would go bald.
Perhaps the reason her heart was so calm was that she had experienced a period of freedom that she could never obtain again?
A freedom that could be described as quite enjoyable.
Or maybe it was thanks to Shara, who was smiling and talking to her in this situation, that she thought for a moment.

But when she delved deeper into the fact that someone could smile and talk to her in this scene, it seemed to lead to an unpleasant realization, so Erika gently averted her gaze from the smiling Sister.
And then Erika Solnzali saw the blue flames.
The quiet morning was a stark contrast to the festive uproar of the previous day.
Thanks to the lord's arrangement, drinks in the town of Hekatai had been free for two days, resulting in a festive atmosphere.
Watching the adventurers sing and dance while treating their injuries, Erika envied their freedom, realizing she was now one of them.

She understood that their hasty revelry stemmed from the knowledge that they might die tomorrow, as they were uncertain about their futures, but she found their lives and that freedom to be appealing.
To live fully and die if one falls short.
What a simple and straightforward way to live.
For Erika, who had lived as the daughter of a marquis, it was as if she were proclaiming her freedom with her very life.
Erika brushed her red hair back as if to gather her thoughts.
While writing a letter as a diary at her desk, Erika thought of the boy who had brought her that freedom.
The boy who had thrown away a proper noble life just to gain acquaintance with her best friend.
If he wanted to gain acquaintance with the Light Priestess, it would be impossible through proper means, given his status as a viscount.
But could one really throw away their life just because they had gained acquaintances?
Just because there were means to reach for what one desired, could one really throw everything away?
At least for her, it was impossible, and Erika wore a self-deprecating smile.
While yearning for freedom, she had given up on such luxuries from the start, being born into a marquis family.
That was why Shin Longdagger appeared so beautiful to her.
Simple, straightforward, and supported by his own free will, his resolve was truly beautiful.
Suddenly, she felt guilty for being by the side of someone like Shin.
At the same time, she reconsidered, thinking that this guilt was not her fault.
Most of this guilt was probably due to Shin Longdagger.
That person was a bit too serious about his role.
Erika thought of the many conversations she had with Shin.
Such kindness and sincerity should be reserved for when she met her best friend.
To casually express such things was a bit much.
Especially to boast about her in public was not good. It was really not good.
She thought it was all an act.
But since he said it so casually in his usual carefree and un-noble manner, it made her heart race.
He was truly capable of anything; she believed he could make a living as an actor.
He was quite handsome as well.
He would surely become popular.
No, no, that's not it.
No, in any case, that was not good. It was really not good, dear husband.
It was a bit of a foe to maidens, throwing out words she wanted to hear at such a delightful timing was borderline criminal.
Also, casually throwing out pleasant words as a surprise should be prohibited.
In other words, the reason she felt a bit flustered was due to Shin Longdagger, and this guilt she felt now was also his fault…
It was definitely not that she liked him or anything.
It was not good, not good at all, Erika Sol… no, Longdagger.
First of all, I am a noble, or rather, I used to be.
What does it matter if I am praised or recognized in front of others?
It makes me extremely happy.
No, no, that's not it.
Erika took a deep breath.
In any case, whatever this feeling is.
──It is something I must repay someday.
Erika Solnzali let out a small, almost thread-like sigh and resumed writing her letter.
A letter to her best friend with no destination.
A moment's hesitation.
Was it a bitter smile or a self-deprecating one?
For a while, I will borrow your boyfriend.
Erika Longdagger concluded her letter.
Erika was at a loss for words as she watched Shin Longdagger, engulfed in blue flames, unleashing them from his entire body within the shattered space.
It was ultra-high purity magical power; the sheer density of magical power alone was causing the phenomenon of magic.
That phenomenon itself had no effect.
However, to be able to create it meant that there was a mastery behind it.
It was a technique that would normally be kept secret, like the secret techniques of the Solnzali family.
The miracle created by operating the magic circle with extreme efficiency was one of the peaks of magical achievement.
The Solnzali family achieved this by using their own hair as a magical power tank, overwhelming efficiency with a vast amount of magical power.
But now, the phenomenon occurring before her was not of that nature.
It was a miracle that arose solely from an individual's talent.
With her mouth agape, Erika was struck dumb by the miracle unfolding before her.
The initial shockwave shattered the large shield Shin had been carrying, and Shara, who had been swaying her head, let out a small cry and fainted.
While gently cradling Shara's head as it fell onto her chest, Erika could not take her eyes off Shin.
Clenching his teeth, with eyes that seemed unsure of where to look, did he realize the miracle he was creating?
[img]https://i.imgur.com/NSzl3LO.jpeg
But one thing was clear; with unwavering certainty, Erika knew that Shin had not given up on living.
The death she had accepted so easily vanished.
She reached out to Shin, who was so close yet so far away.
Did this unserious former classmate know that the true nature of Rainibati No. 5 would manifest after the shockwave that would cleanse this land?
That the very shattered space would drain magical power from all living beings within its range and reap their lives?
Her outstretched hand touched Shin's cheek.
"…I will believe in you, my Longdagger."
Erika felt her meager magical power being absorbed the moment it touched the blue flames.
Was it being absorbed by the Church?
As she resisted the rapidly approaching, irresistible drowsiness, she followed its destination.
In her fading consciousness, she felt a sensation of being enveloped, and Erika regretted that her hand was leaving Shin's cheek.
She set down her pen, placed the letter in an envelope, and sealed it.
The breath that escaped her mouth was either from the fatigue of finishing her writing or something else entirely; even Erika herself could not tell.
But there was no doubt that it was mixed with exasperation at Shin's un-noble behavior, as he was shouting loudly in another room.
Goodness, my husband is utterly lax for a noble.
To be able to perform such a remarkable technique, yet to easily raise his voice and panic.
He should consider his own abilities more objectively and seriously.
As Erika stood up from her chair, she smiled wryly.
Well, he claimed he hardly remembered what had happened in that hole, so perhaps it couldn't be helped.
He even said he didn't remember the words he had spoken, which might have been his last, so Shin might indeed be a foe to maidens.
Well, she was grateful that he had forgotten.
Still, what on earth was he making such a fuss about?
As Erika opened the door, she became aware of her heart racing.
She made sure her voice wouldn’t bounce.
With a truly challenging smile, she said, wondering what would happen next.
"What on earth are you making such a fuss about, dear husband?"
